items.q: Confirmation that all these works have been undertaken?
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL.** Greenway characterises the works as done: it "reviewed the extent of works done to
body:
**PARTIAL.** Greenway characterises the works as done: it "reviewed the extent of works done to
the Grade-I-listed Main House", comparing "the condition of the building before the works were
carried out and the condition of the building as of today", and prices "transforming the
building to its current state of repair" (Greenway p. 5). That is an estimate of works already
reflected in the building, not a record of expenditure — there are no invoices, contracts,
contractor name, dates, completion certificates or warranties, and the report is priced at
Q2 2026 rates rather than at the time of the works (Greenway pp. 5–6).

Scope is narrower than the question assumes. The figures cover the **Main House only** and
exclude expenditure over the same period on the Riding School, the courtyard, the chapel, the
gate house buildings, other building or perimeter/security elements, the waterway, the
Capability Brown landscape conservation works, and the demolition of non-listed elements
already removed (Greenway p. 5).

*Ask:* invoices/contracts substantiating the £40.26m, and the equivalent record for the
buildings Greenway excludes.

**PARTIAL.** Nothing in Greenway. But JSA records the position as at 2021: the buildings "make

items.q: Has the asbestos work/removal been done?
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL.** Two separate pieces of evidence, neither conclusive.
body: **PARTIAL.** Two separate pieces of evidence, neither conclusive.

- Main House: "Asbestos Removal, 3,855 m², £52/m², **£200,000**" sits within Enabling works in

- Courtyards: the 2021 application "is also accompanied by a **Type 3 Asbestos Survey**. The

Neither the survey, nor any clearance certificate, air test, or asbestos register, is in the
room.

type, so this is close to what is being asked for, but: it is five years old, it covers the
**courtyards only**, and it is not in the room. No management survey, and nothing at all for
the Main House.

items.statusLine: **PARTIAL.** Cost evidence for the Main House — "Roof Works, 3,855 m², £311/m², **£1,200,000**"

items.q: There is reference to the flood plain and specifically the area changing, hence relocating some of the houses. Are there details for this?
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL — and the two sources in the room point in opposite directions.**
body: **PARTIAL — and the two sources in the room point in opposite directions.**

The claim the question refers to is Savills': "Construction in the Meadows will not be impeded
by the existing floodplain. We have been informed that **the existing masterplan is incorrect
and the floodplains are far smaller than is currently shown. This is currently being updated by
the environment agency**" (Savills p. 47). It recurs as an assumption behind the unit
positioning: "These recommendations are based on the assumption that the floodplain in the
southwestern corner of the meadows has no material impact on the areas of the site which are
suitable for construction. We understand that the environment agency are in the process of
updating these flood zones" (Savills p. 50). At plot level: Meadows North contains "a small
pond in this area which also falls within a flood area, reducing the area for development,
however these flood maps are being updated, and the pond may be removed"; Riverside North /
Woodlands is "restricted by the density of woodlands, listed monuments and the floodplain";
Riverside South "is relatively clear and is not restricted by trees or floodplains"
(Savills p. 11).

Against that, the only primary flood evidence in the room is older and harder: the *Flood Risk
Assessment and Drainage Strategy* prepared by **RAB in February 2021**, quoted verbatim in JSA
§2.7 — "The proposed development at Fawley Court, Henley-on-Thames, RG9 3AE is located in
**Flood Zone 3**, as defined in the NPPF … the site is shown to have a **medium-high groundwater
vulnerability** … To mitigate the risk of fluvial flooding during the 1% AEP + 35% climate
change event, it is proposed to raise the finished floor level … (a minimum of **33.22 mAOD**) …
The proposed development must incorporate SuDS as described in Section 5.4."

What is missing: the RAB report itself, any Environment Agency correspondence, any revised flood
map or modelling, and any dated confirmation that the zones have in fact been updated. Note
also that EPR's own constraints drawing lists only two site-wide constraints — the Grade II*
Registered Park and Garden and the Fawley Court Conservation Area — and **does not map a
floodplain at all** (Site Plan p. 1). Align's own annotation on Masterplan CK reads "Check for
flood plain" against the south-eastern strip of the housing zone.

*Ask, precisely:* the RAB FRA, and the EA evidence for the re-mapping — a date, a reference, or
a copy of the revised zone plan. Savills' entire 12-unit positioning rests on it.

items.q: Are there more detailed plans and cost assessments for the new areas, such as the spa, to allow us to do a more detailed assessment?
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL.** Plans: concept level only. The spa/wellness is the Concert Hall (the deconsecrated
body:
**PARTIAL.** Plans: concept level only. The spa/wellness is the Concert Hall (the deconsecrated
church, described in the room as the Pavilion), and the room gives its area split — "Concert
Hall - Wellness + 50sqm mezzanine 471 sqm" plus "**New Concert Hall 2-storey Extension 529
sqm**", totalling 1,000 sqm / 10,763.90 sq ft (Area Schedule rows 58–61) — and one preliminary
perspective sketch, "Preliminary designs for addition to Pavilion at Fawley Court"
(Brochure p. 11). There is no plan, no section, no schedule of accommodation for the spa.
Costs: none, for the spa or for any other new area. See also New Development item 1d.

items.q: In terms of working on the extensions that are part of existing building, is there access to structural assessments to ensure that these work?
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL — assessments exist and are named; none is in the room.** JSA cites, for the courtyard
body:
**PARTIAL — assessments exist and are named; none is in the room.** JSA cites, for the courtyard
group: "*Courtyard Buildings and Gatehouse: Structural Engineering Appraisal of the Existing
Structure with Comments on the Implications of the Proposed Alterations and Associated
Drawings*" by **Alan Baxter and Associates** (JSA §2.6); "*Buildings Survey Report*" by
**William Martin & Partners LLP** for current building conditions (§2.5); and "*A Historic
Building Survey of Service Buildings at Fawley Court*" by **Kirsty Rodwell** plus "*Fawley Court
Conservation Plan Vols. 1-3*" by **Dr Sarah Rutherford** (§2.4, §1.5). JSA §6.4 reports the
structural survey's conclusions for the Riding School roof. Historic England's 2010 letter
confirms the same appraisal was live then: "English Heritage will need to be satisfied that the
stability of the structure as a whole is not compromised by this restoration and I am encouraged
to hear that Baxters are investigating this issue" (JSA Appendix II, p. 24).

The consent itself makes structural detail a pre-commencement gate: before any works to the
Riding School, a method statement for the structural reinforcement process "with regard to the
movement within the Riding School", a copy of the timber specialist's report, and the
methodology for the reinforcing ply diaphragm including eaves and fixing details, must be
approved (LBC condition 3, p. 2); and before works to the historic courtyard walls and laundry
building, an internal-reinforcement methodology (condition 6, p. 3).

Nothing whatever exists for the Main House, its basement, or the **Proposed South Wing** — the
extension "part of existing building" the question is most likely aimed at.

items.q: Utilities - power, gas, water, Wi-Fi, drainage - local capacity and infrastructure details would be useful (particularly to allow for extension plans)
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL, and thin.** What the room gives:
body: **PARTIAL, and thin.** What the room gives:

- **Foul drainage:** "There are no public sewers on site. At present foul drainage is discharged
  to various cess pits across the estate and is periodically collected and taken off site to be
  disposed of at a sewage treatment facility. There is no proposed change to the current foul
  sewage drainage system" (JSA §2.8).
- **Surface water:** SuDS required per the RAB strategy; an underground water storage tank is
  indicated on drawings PL306 and PL320 (JSA §2.7).
- **Heat:** oil heating "recently been totally upgraded"; a water-based heat pump system to serve
  the main buildings has permission and is part implemented; the courtyard scheme proposes a
  geothermal heat pump (JSA §3.5). Savills understands "the existing house is sustainable in
  terms of both heating and water, by harnessing the energy from the River Thames"
  (Savills p. 10).
- **Water conservation:** dual-flush and self-closing taps, grey water harvested from roofs for
  irrigation (JSA §13.6).

What is missing: everything the question actually asks for. No capacity statements from any
utility, no incoming supply records, no metering data, no gas position, no potable water
infrastructure, no telecoms or Wi-Fi provision, no drainage survey (JSA §6.15 only proposes that
"an investigation of below ground drainage will be carried out"). Align's own Masterplan CK
mark-up posits two new sub-stations and two power-supply routes — that is Align's hypothesis,
not vendor evidence.

items.q: Has any work been carried out on possible usage of utilities upon completion of the works?
items.statusLine: **NOT IN ROOM.** No demand study, no load assessment, no energy model for the completed hotel.
body:
**NOT IN ROOM.** No demand study, no load assessment, no energy model for the completed hotel.
The Ecovision *Energy Report* named at JSA §3.5 relates to the 2021 courtyard scheme and is not
in the room in any event.

items.statusLine: **NOT IN ROOM.** No condition or capacity survey of existing MEP systems. Greenway's single-line
body:
**NOT IN ROOM.** No condition or capacity survey of existing MEP systems. Greenway's single-line
MEP allowance (p. 8) is a cost, not a survey; the named Ecovision report is an energy report,
not a survey of existing systems.

items.q: Fire risk assessment will need to be carried out. Measures were agreed by Building Control, were they followed out?
items.statusLine: **NOT IN ROOM.** No fire risk assessment, no building control correspondence, no evidence of
body:
**NOT IN ROOM.** No fire risk assessment, no building control correspondence, no evidence of
agreed measures or their execution. As with Historic Construction Costs item 6, the premise
("measures were agreed by Building Control") is not corroborated by anything in the room.

items.q: Fire exits – have these been signed off by the architects as adequate?
items.statusLine: **NOT IN ROOM.** No egress strategy, no architect's sign-off. JSA states an intention only — the
body:
**NOT IN ROOM.** No egress strategy, no architect's sign-off. JSA states an intention only — the
restoration and courtyards "provides the opportunity to make these areas fully accessible, allow
them to function safely and independently in terms of accessibility and emergency egress"
(JSA §12.1.1). An intention in a 2021 design statement is not a sign-off, and it does not cover
the Main House.

items.q: Sewage Capacity – SuDs and cess pits combination, have these been sized by an engineer? What about for the new accommodation?
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL.** The arrangement is confirmed and it is a cess-pit-and-tanker system with no mains
body:
**PARTIAL.** The arrangement is confirmed and it is a cess-pit-and-tanker system with no mains
connection: "There are no public sewers on site … foul drainage is discharged to various cess
pits across the estate and is periodically collected and taken off site … **There is no proposed
change to the current foul sewage drainage system**" (JSA §2.8). SuDS were sized by an engineer
for the 2021 courtyard scheme — "The proposed development must incorporate SuDS as described in
Section 5.4 of this report" (RAB, quoted at JSA §2.7) — but Section 5.4 and the report itself
are not in the room, and the sizing was for a scheme of staff flats, estate offices, a pool and
15 guest rooms, not 60 keys plus 12 houses plus events.

Nothing in the room sizes foul capacity, tankering frequency or treatment for the proposed
scheme. Given "no proposed change to the current foul sewage drainage system" is the position of
record, this is a material and under-appreciated cost and consent risk.

items.q: Reference to rooms going from 13 to 17 (1 on st floor, 2 on second floor) - does this having LBC?
items.statusLine: **ANSWERED — no, and the room is unambiguous.** The only listed building consent in the room is
body:
**ANSWERED — no, and the room is unambiguous.** The only listed building consent in the room is
23/07590/LBC, granted 6 December 2024, and its consented description is confined to the
courtyard group: "Restoration of grade II listed riding school, restoration of grade II listed
chapel, dairy and service courtyards, restoration of clock and water tower, construction of new
estate office, staff and guest accommodation and demolition of existing derelict structures"
(LBC p. 1). It does not touch the Main House. Its FUL companion **23/07589/FUL is not in the
data room at all** — the single largest consent gap. Savills confirms the wider position:
"An application has not yet been submitted to add an additional wing to the main house"
(Savills p. 7).
Two corrections to the question itself, both from the room:

- The count is **four** new rooms, not three. EPR's own annotation on the Main House key sheet
  reads "**was 13**" against the 17-key schedule, with "**1 new on 1st; 3 on 2nd**" and
  "Additional room" / "Additional rooms" arrows to the specific rooms (Key Plans p. 9). The
  question's "(1 on st floor, 2 on second floor)" understates the plan by one room.
- The two Main House schedules in the room do not agree. The brochure schedule (rev B,
  10/07/2025) totals the Main House at **1,815 sqm** with a single 135 sqm Principal Suite on the
  first floor (Brochure p. 12); the standalone spreadsheet totals **2,202 sqm**, shows
  "2 x 135sqm Principal Suite" on the first floor and adds a 127 sqm "New wing F&B Ballroom /
  lounge" (Area Schedule rows 12, 20, 33). Both still print 17 keys.

items.q: Pool now a distance from the hotel, as is gym
items.statusLine: **ANSWERED as to fact and reason; the distance itself is not stated anywhere.** Both are in the
body:
**ANSWERED as to fact and reason; the distance itself is not stated anywhere.** Both are in the
South Courtyard, in the service-courtyard group north-west of the Main House, and the reason is
explicit: "Functional spaces required for a building of this type, which preferably would not be
incorporated into a Grade I listed historic structure such as a swimming pool" (JSA §1.6.3), and
"The incorporation of the gym and sauna in the South Courtyard means that the Grade I listed
Main Building need not be altered to accommodate them" (JSA §7.7).

Detail: "The South Courtyard will provide space for pool, gym and spa facilities, estate
security, office space and 15 guest rooms" (JSA §7.1); the Pool House to the north is "a double
height space with an indoor swimming and plunge pools with spa areas included in the east
range", with a small brick extension at the eastern end housing pool plant (§7.3); the gym is
"a double height gym with access to the sauna at ground floor level" in the eastern range
(§7.7). The Masterplan annotation marks "gym", "Pool" and "spa" over the Consented South
Courtyard (Masterplan p. 1).

Note the 2025 scheme moves the spa away again — to the Concert Hall/Pavilion at the far south of
the estate (Area Schedule rows 58–61; Brochure p. 10) — so pool, gym and spa are now proposed in
two different locations, both remote from the Main House. Savills records the same lack of
resolution: the Concert Hall is for "either a spa or restaurant use" and the old riding
school/stables for "a spa or other amenity / ancillary use" (Savills p. 9).

items.q: Staff accommodation and staff canteen now moved to the gate houses
items.statusLine: **ANSWERED — and the room exposes a three-way conflict worth raising on the call.**
body: **ANSWERED — and the room exposes a three-way conflict worth raising on the call.**

- **The 2025 EPR scheme** does put staff in the lodges and gatehouses: "LODGES (STAFF FACILITIES
  + BOH)" totalling **709 sqm / 7,631.61 sq ft** — North Lodge 139, North Lodge Extension 75,
  New North Gatehouses (2 × 90) 180, New South Gatehouses (2 × 90) 180, Existing South Lodge 75,
  New South Lodge 60 (Area Schedule rows 62–69). Masterplan CK labels "Staff accommodation" at
  both the North Lodge and the southern gatehouses.
- **The staff canteen is not in the gatehouses.** It is drawn in the Stables: "Prep kitchen" and
  "Staff canteen/wc" inside the 184 sqm Back of House building immediately north of the Riding
  School restaurant (Key Plans p. 11; Area Schedule row 72).
- **The consented position is different again.** Under the 2024 LBC scheme, staff accommodation,
  storage and staff dining sit in the **North Courtyard** and the Old Stable Block: "Staff
  accommodation space and storage areas are to be relocated in the new North Courtyard to the
  east" (JSA §6.2); "The northern building incorporates a full range of staff flats with a first
  floor accessed via an external stair" and "the rest of the east wing and the entirety of the
  west range are made up of staff accommodation" (§8.2–8.3); the Old Stable Block "will be
  renovated to provide kitchen, laundry, staff dining facilities and WCs" (§10.1). Those are
  precisely the buildings the 2025 scheme converts to guest rooms.

EPR flags the same problem on its own drawing, in capitals: "**WHERE DOES STAFF ACCOMMODATION &
STORAGE GO NOW BEDROOMS IN NORTH COURTYARD?**" (Key Plans p. 11). Masterplan CK annotates the
North Courtyard "20 Guest rooms - new build" and the South Courtyard "23 Guest rooms - amend
existing build".

The consequence for consent is the substantive point: the courtyards are labelled "Consented" on
the masterplan, but what is consented there is staff flats, storage and estate offices — not 43
guest rooms.

items.q: Is the pavilion used for the regatta subject to a temporary licence? Has a discussion on a more permanent licence been considered?
items.statusLine: **NOT IN ROOM.** There is no licence, licensing correspondence, premises licence, or event
body:
**NOT IN ROOM.** There is no licence, licensing correspondence, premises licence, or event
consent of any kind in the data room. The statement in the question traces to Align's own
annotation on Masterplan CK — "Pavillion - weddings and private events - **currently only temp
licence**" — not to a vendor document.

What the room does show: the scheme itself treats the Regatta structure as temporary —
"Regatta Temporary Pavilion (200-500 pax)", 500 sqm (Area Schedule row 75) — alongside a 75 sqm
"Riverside Floating Restaurant" (row 74) and, in the brochure revision, "various events
marquees — tbc" (Brochure p. 12). The 2017 River Club brochure evidences a five-day Regatta
hospitality operation (Wednesday 28 June – Sunday 2 July 2017) with a restaurant, lounge viewing
decks and the floating "Long Water Bar", but states no capacities, no pricing and no licensing
basis (`2.5.1`, cluster index E). Separately, Henley Royal Regatta owns the land immediately in
front of the site (Savills p. 10) and holds a 999-year lease of Temple Island granted in 1986
(`2.6.1` History, p. 93).

*Ask:* the current premises licence(s), any temporary event notices used to date, and the
licensing history — this underpins a revenue line and is currently unevidenced.

items.q: Spa at 1,000m2 is a little small, would want to nudge up by 20%, and possibly add external garden area if possible.
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL — the 1,000 sqm is confirmed and, importantly, over half of it is already new build.**
body:
**PARTIAL — the 1,000 sqm is confirmed and, importantly, over half of it is already new build.**
The split is "Concert Hall - Wellness + 50sqm mezzanine **471 sqm**" plus "New Concert Hall
2-storey Extension **529 sqm**" = 1,000 sqm / 10,763.90 sq ft (Area Schedule rows 58–61). A 20%
uplift is therefore a 200 sqm enlargement of a new-build extension attached to a building within
a Grade II* Registered Park and Conservation Area, not a fit-out variation — a consent question
before it is a cost question. Masterplan CK carries the same instruction: "Spa - needs to be
200m2 bigger" and "Ideally to include spa garden".

**No external spa garden appears anywhere** in the area schedule or on any masterplan. The
nearest adjacencies drawn are "Reinstate loggia" and "Reinstate South Pleasure Gardens", with
Align's own "Yoga deck?" annotation over the loggia (Masterplan CK). And the vendor's own
advisers had not fixed which building the spa occupies — Concert Hall for "either a spa or
restaurant use", old riding school/stables for "a spa or other amenity" (Savills p. 9).

items.q: Are there more detailed design plans and cost assessments for:
body:
*No cost assessment exists for any of the five. There is no forward cost plan of any kind in the
data room — see "Hotel Development" item 4 in the second half. The design position differs by
building:*

items.q: …the new bedroom wing
items.statusLine: **NOT IN ROOM.** The "Proposed South Wing" appears only as a coloured footprint on the masterplan
body:
**NOT IN ROOM.** The "Proposed South Wing" appears only as a coloured footprint on the masterplan
(Masterplan p. 1; Brochure p. 7), with Align's own annotation "9 bedrooms" (Masterplan CK). The
area schedule carries a single related line, "New wing F&B Ballroom / lounge 127 sqm"
(Area Schedule row 12) — and that line is absent from the earlier brochure revision
(Brochure p. 12), so even the use is unsettled. No plan, no elevation, no section, no schedule
of accommodation. Consent position: "An application has not yet been submitted to add an
additional wing to the main house" (Savills p. 7).

Note the key-count consequence: 17 Main House + 43 Stables = 60 keys (Key Plans pp. 6, 10;
Area Schedule A1). If the South Wing carries nine bedrooms, the scheme is 69, not 60. Savills
describes it as adding "further hotel keys based on the preferences of the chosen operator"
(Savills p. 9) and gives the whole as a 65-key hotel (p. 9) — a third figure. The room contains
no reconciled key count.

items.q: …the Courtyard
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL.** The consented design exists and is identified drawing by drawing, but the drawings
body:
**PARTIAL.** The consented design exists and is identified drawing by drawing, but the drawings
are not in the room. LBC condition 2 lists the approved set: "21-01/A; PL300D; PL301C; PL302C;
PL303B; PL304B; PL305D; PL306C; PL320C; PL321C; PL322B; PV300B … PV340; SL10C; SL11B; SL12B;
SL326A; SL327; SL328; SL329; and SL330" (LBC p. 2). The 2021 Design & Access Statement describes
the scheme building by building (JSA §§5.1–5.4, 7.1–7.11, 8.1–8.8) and reproduces South Courtyard
and Riding School elevations, original and adjusted (JSA pp. 27–28). The 2025 re-use as 43 guest
rooms is drawn only at concept level (Key Plans pp. 11–12).
*Ask:* the approved drawing set named in condition 2.

items.q: …the Riding School

**NOT IN ROOM.** Nothing on dredging, silt levels, the Long Water, the inlet, or navigation. The

items.q: There is no design for the houses, only the sizes
items.statusLine: **ANSWERED — the observation is correct, and the room is more specific than "sizes".** What
body:
**ANSWERED — the observation is correct, and the room is more specific than "sizes".** What
exists (all Savills, October 2025, non-Red-Book and expressly "not a formal valuation",
pp. 2, 58):

- Quantum and mix: "a maximum of **12 new branded residences**. The unit mix comprises **5-bed
  and 6-bed houses only**" (p. 57) — five 5-bed in the Meadows, three 6-bed Riverside
  North/Woodlands, four 6-bed Riverside South (pp. 5, 51).
- Sizes: "the 5-bed units have a GIA of **5,200 sq ft** while the 6-beds are **5,700 sq ft**"
  (p. 51); 65,900 sq ft in total.
- Plots: "a private plot of a minimum 1-1.5 acres" (pp. 5, 50).
- Positions: twelve numbered positions across three zones on a masterplan extract (p. 50), with
  zone areas — Meadows North ~4.5 acres, Meadows ~8 acres, Riverside North/Woodlands ~3 acres,
  Riverside South ~5 acres (p. 11).
- A design brief, but not a design: minimum 3m ceiling heights, lockable storage, all bedrooms
  en-suite, a wine room, prep-kitchen and multi-functional gym/study space, service access to the
  back kitchen "thus avoiding the main entrance", air-conditioning, underfloor heating and smart
  home control, traditional/historic exterior with locally sourced materials and a modern
  internal layout (p. 55).
- Tenure: **"The properties will all be sold on long leasehold titles (999 years) with a private
  garden allocated to each unit"** (p. 47). This sits against the deal's freehold assumption and
  remains an open structuring ruling.

EPR shows only an indicative housing zone (Brochure p. 7); Align's own Masterplan CK marks twelve
house positions as blue dots. No architect is appointed for the houses — Savills assumes
"Architecture, interior design, exterior design and landscaping will all be carried out by
internationally recognised professionals of the highest calibre" (p. 47).

items.q: Can we build an outline cost assessment on this basis?
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL.** The room supplies unit count, GIA per unit, total GIA, plot sizes, indicative
body:
**PARTIAL.** The room supplies unit count, GIA per unit, total GIA, plot sizes, indicative
positions, specification requirements and a sustainability target ("aimed to be net zero …
sustainable heating and water harnessed from the Thames", p. 55), plus Savills' amenity split
between private and shared (p. 56, including covered garage parking private to each house and a
private outdoor pool per house, p. 54).

It supplies none of: a design, levels or cut-and-fill, ground conditions (the only ground
document is a named but unsupplied **Phase 1 Contamination Assessment**, JSA §13.5 — a desk study,
not a ground investigation), tree constraints at plot level, flood levels for the Meadows,
acoustic mitigation design, infrastructure routes, or a build programme. Savills' own
qualification: "All of the recommended buildable area is above ground" (p. 47).

body:
**NOT IN ROOM.** Scope is specified without cost: each house on a 1–1.5 acre plot with "a
landscaped private garden, allocated directly outside the Property … completely private space for

items.statusLine: **NOT IN ROOM.** No cost. Savills' assumption is net-zero houses with heating and water harnessed
body:
**NOT IN ROOM.** No cost. Savills' assumption is net-zero houses with heating and water harnessed
from the Thames (pp. 10, 55) — a river-source scheme that has never been costed, permitted or

items.q: Need for sound protection/fencing given the noisy road
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL — the problem is well evidenced; the mitigation is assumed, not designed.**
body: **PARTIAL — the problem is well evidenced; the mitigation is assumed, not designed.**

Evidence of the problem: "The site experiences road noise from the A4155, particularly in the
southern part of the site where the residences are proposed to be built. There is also often
heavy traffic on this road which, at certain times of day, can back up outside the main entrance
to Fawley Court" (Savills p. 10). Three of the four development zones are affected: Meadows
North, Meadows and Meadows South each "on the western edge of the site, backing onto the Marlow
Road (A4155) and subject to significant road noise" (p. 11). "The road noise is a key threat and
disturbance to the site, significantly impeding on the sense of peace and tranquillity expected
in a rural property" (p. 47).

Mitigation: an assumption — "Following extensive acoustic tests and noise cancellation
strategies, road noise in the Meadows area will be significantly reduced" (p. 47) — and an
expectation — "Noise mitigation strategies are expected to include planting additional trees,
hedge laying, water features and **building a wall on the site boundary**. Extra consideration
should be made for seasonal changes, when there may be less privacy and increased road noise due
to deciduous trees shedding their leaves" (p. 54).

**No acoustic test, survey or assessment exists in the room** — for the residences or for the
hotel. This is the same gap as Historic Construction Costs item 12.

items.q: Need power supply as cannot have oil fired. Drainage if not on mains sewer?
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL — the drainage limb is answered definitively; the power limb is not.**
body: **PARTIAL — the drainage limb is answered definitively; the power limb is not.**

*Drainage — answered:* there is **no mains sewer**. "There are no public sewers on site. At
present foul drainage is discharged to various cess pits across the estate and is periodically
collected and taken off site to be disposed of at a sewage treatment facility. There is no
proposed change to the current foul sewage drainage system" (JSA §2.8). Any residential scheme
needs either a package treatment plant with a discharge consent, a new mains connection, or an
extension of the tankering arrangement — none of which is addressed anywhere in the room.

*Power — not answered:* the current position is that estate buildings ran on oil, "recently been
totally upgraded", with a water-based heat pump system permitted and part implemented, and a
geothermal heat pump proposed for the courtyards (JSA §3.5). Savills assumes Thames-sourced
heating and water for the houses (pp. 10, 55). There is no grid capacity statement, no DNO
correspondence, no connection agreement and no load assessment. Align's own Masterplan CK
mark-up posits two sub-stations and two supply routes — a hypothesis, not evidence.

items.q: There doesn't appear to be too many difficult conditions other than materials and sign off by heritage.
items.statusLine: **ANSWERED for the consent that is in the room — but that consent is half the picture.**
body: **ANSWERED for the consent that is in the room — but that consent is half the picture.**

The reading is correct for 23/07590/LBC. All seven conditions are in the room verbatim
(LBC pp. 1–3):

1. Works to begin within three years of the consent date — i.e. **by 6 December 2027**.
2. Build in accordance with the approved application and the listed drawings (set out in full at
   LBC p. 2), unless otherwise agreed in writing.
3. **Pre-commencement (Riding School):** method statement for the structural reinforcement
   process "with regard to the movement within the Riding School"; the timber specialist's report
   on timbers requiring replacement; methodology for the reinforcing ply diaphragm to the
   internal roof, including eaves details and fixing methods.
4. **Pre-external-finish:** schedule and/or samples of materials and finishes including rainwater
   goods, mortar and pointing. For the avoidance of doubt — black cast aluminium rainwater goods;
   slate roof coverings as existing with existing slates reused where possible; new brickwork
   matching existing in tone, dimensions, colour and bond; traditional lime mortar and pointing;
   **a sample panel of brickwork and mortar constructed on site and retained for the duration of
   the works**; no paint removal from external historic brickwork without an approved methodology
   statement.
5. **Pre-installation (joinery):** full door and window schedule with 1:20 and 1:5 sectional
   drawings showing profiles and depths of glazing bars, sills, reveals and glazing; all windows
   and doors timber; ironmongery details; casements vertically hung, flush fitting, without
   quarter light openings or trickle vents; window units installed with lime mortar — "spray foam
   is unacceptable".
6. **Pre-commencement (historic courtyard walls and laundry building):** internal reinforcement
   methodology and materials.
7. **Pre-commencement (internal works, including insulation):** schedule/details of all works;
   all internal walls of existing and restored historic structures to be lime plastered unless
   otherwise agreed.

**No section 106, no CIL, no ecology, no highways, no parking, no drainage, no landscape and no
hours-of-use condition** appears on this notice. Three of the seven are pre-commencement gates,
and nothing in the room evidences that any has been discharged or that works have commenced.

The qualification: this is the **listed building consent only**. Its companion **23/07589/FUL is
not in the data room**, and the FUL is where ecology, highways, drainage, landscape, materials
for non-listed elements and operational conditions normally sit. The masterplan labels the
courtyards "Consented" (Masterplan p. 2), but on the strength of the LBC alone that label cannot
be verified for the FUL, and nothing establishes a lawful hotel use.

items.q: Is there any paperwork regarding the pre-app discussions?
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL — one pre-app response is in the room in full; nothing for the current schemes.**
body: **PARTIAL — one pre-app response is in the room in full; nothing for the current schemes.**

Reproduced verbatim at JSA Appendix II (pp. 24–26): the English Heritage pre-application advice
letter, our ref **PA00013192**, dated **5 July 2010**, from **Richard Peats**, Historic Buildings
and Areas Adviser, to **Mr John Phillips of Phillips Planning Services Ltd**, copied to
**Martin Andrew, Conservation Officer, Wycombe District Council**, following a site meeting on
24 June 2010 with the client and Marcus Binney. JSA records two pre-app submissions: one across
the Fawley Court Estate in **August 2009** (response ref EH/PA00010803, §4.1) and one in
**June 2010** on more detailed drawings (§3.2). The adjusted elevations produced in response are
at JSA pp. 27–28.

What is missing: any pre-app paperwork for the **2023 applications** (23/07589/FUL and
23/07590/LBC), for the **2025 EPR 60-key scheme**, or for the **residential**. On the residential
Savills reports only hearsay: "Pre-application discussions have taken place for the development
of residences in the grounds, and we understand that these have been, so far, well-received
however, an application has yet to be made" (Savills p. 7). No note, letter, minute or officer
response sits behind that sentence anywhere in the room — and it is load-bearing for the entire
enabling-development case.

items.q: Are there any particular designs for the new build / specific direction the planners want?
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL — for the courtyard group the direction is in the room in detail; for everything else
body:
**PARTIAL — for the courtyard group the direction is in the room in detail; for everything else
there is none.**

Historic England's 2010 letter (JSA pp. 24–26) gives specific direction: restoring the riding
school's original form is "of greater value than retaining the later fabric" and full restoration
of the original window form "is considered to be the best option"; no objection in principle "to
the principle of creating two courtyards of service buildings on the site of the current service
building courts"; restoration of the chapel "welcomed"; the WWII-era and later buildings
south-west of the house should be removed "in due course… to allow the restoration of the
landscape"; **"Any application should therefore be accompanied by a master plan that places the
need for these buildings in the context of how the estate as a whole is to be managed. It should
also provide a clear rationale outlining why the level of accommodation provided is necessary"**;
on materials, the exterior was "bare brick laid in a Flemish bond with dark red stretchers and
blue headers", lime-washing may be the best way to a unified finish, and paint striping must be
carried out with extreme care; on design, the south elevation centrepiece "does look a little
odd", the first floor window level "looks a little uncomfortable", a plat band or simple plinth
would be worth considering, the veranda's "rather vernacular looking timber posts and arch
braces… do not work well with the classical buildings at the north and south ends", and the lower
part of the west wall of the dairy wing must be retained.

LBC conditions 4, 5 and 7 then codify materials, joinery and internal finishes (see item 1).
JSA §5.6 states the resulting palette: Flemish bond brickwork, slate roofs, generally two storeys,
painted timber sash windows, painted cast aluminium rainwater goods.

Nothing exists for the new houses, the South Wing, the Concert Hall extension or the gatehouses
beyond two preliminary sketches (Brochure p. 11).

items.q: Any ecological requirements been mentioned in relation to planning? Set out in the conditions
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL.** **23/07590/LBC carries no ecological condition** (LBC pp. 1–3) — as would be normal
body:
**PARTIAL.** **23/07590/LBC carries no ecological condition** (LBC pp. 1–3) — as would be normal
for a listed building consent; ecology conditions would sit on the FUL, which is absent from the
room.

Ecological work exists and is named: "An Ecological Survey has been carried out on the site.
Please refer to *Ecological Scoping Survey* prepared by **Aspect Ecology** and an updated report
prepared by **Catherine Bickmore**" (JSA §13.4). A BS5837 tree survey has also been carried out
"in accordance with the council requirements" — "there are no Grade A or veteran trees on site …
none of the important trees highlighted by Christopher Gallagher are affected by the proposals
and tree removals are limited to shrubs and small self seeded trees" (JSA §2.9, §3.4, §5.8.2).
None of these reports is in the room, and all predate the 2023 applications and the 2025 scheme.

No biodiversity net gain assessment or metric is in the room. Any fresh application for the
60-key scheme or the residences would engage mandatory BNG, and the registered park, woodland
and river corridor make that a live design and land-take constraint, not a form-filling exercise.

items.q: Any conditions available? Mainly heritage confirmation of materials
items.statusLine: **ANSWERED.** Yes — the full decision notice for 23/07590/LBC is in the room with all seven
body:
**ANSWERED.** Yes — the full decision notice for 23/07590/LBC is in the room with all seven
conditions and their reasons set out verbatim (LBC pp. 1–3; see item 1 above for the list).
Materials is indeed the operative external condition (condition 4), and heritage sign-off runs
through conditions 3 to 7. Decision dated 6 December 2024, signed Eric Owens, Service Director of
Planning & Environment; Decision Making Officer Ray Martin, Case Officer Heather Smith; applicant
**Cherrilow Limited**, agent Phillips Planning Services Limited (LBC pp. 1, 4).

No conditions are available for any other consent. The seven older minor-works notices
(15/05907, 15/05908, 17/05210, 17/05211, 18/05598, 18/05599, 15/07051) are in the room as scanned
notices; all are permissions to Cherrilow Limited carrying standard three-year commencement
conditions, and **all of their commencement deadlines have passed** — the latest on 26 April 2021
(cluster index B, vision mop-up). And the FUL's conditions are unseen.

items.q: Has bat, soil, traffic surveys been commissioned?
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL — two of the three were commissioned; none is in the room; the third has no trace.**
body: **PARTIAL — two of the three were commissioned; none is in the room; the third has no trace.**

- **Soil:** yes, in part. "A Land Contamination report has been carried out to identify issues
  regarding land contamination on site. Please refer to the *Phase 1 Contamination Assessment*
  prepared by **Opus Joynes Pike**" (JSA §13.5). Not supplied. A Phase 1 is a desk study — there
  is no ground investigation, no sampling, no geotechnical or bearing-capacity data anywhere in
  the room, for the courtyards or for the housing zones.
- **Bat:** an *Ecological Scoping Survey* by **Aspect Ecology** and an update by **Catherine
  Bickmore** are named (JSA §13.4). Neither is supplied, and neither is stated to include bat
  emergence or activity surveys. A Grade I house, a chapel, a derelict water tower and derelict
  timber outbuildings would ordinarily require them, and their season (roughly May to September)
  puts them on the critical path for any application.
- **Traffic:** **no trace at all.** No transport assessment, no travel plan, no traffic survey, no
  highways correspondence. Savills records that traffic on the A4155 "at certain times of day, can
  back up outside the main entrance to Fawley Court" (p. 10). The 2015 access consent
  15/07051/FUL carried access-first sequencing and visibility-splay conditions (cluster index B,
  vision mop-up), whose discharge is unevidenced and whose commencement deadline passed on
  23 September 2018.

items.q: Do the floor plans work as a hotel? They appear to.
items.statusLine: **JUDGMENT** (operator and architect). What the room gives: existing Main House plans for
body:
**JUDGMENT** (operator and architect). What the room gives: existing Main House plans for
basement, ground, mezzanine, first and second floors (`2.3.1`–`2.3.5`) with whole-floor GIAs —
basement 1,475.2 sqm / 15,878.9 sq ft **including tunnels**, ground 877.2 sqm / 9,442.1 sq ft,
mezzanine 54.4 sqm / 585.5 sq ft **excluding stairwells**, first 820.5 sqm / 8,831.7 sq ft,
second 866.8 sqm / 9,330.8 sq ft **including eave space** — plus EPR's room-by-room key plans and
the area schedule.

Two health warnings that bear on any judgment made from them. First, the inclusion bases are
inconsistent floor to floor, so the plans do not aggregate. Second, and more seriously, the
existing plans are not measured: the first and second floor drawings state that details are
"taken from proposed design drawings, were not measured on site and should be viewed as
approximate" (Floor Plans `2.3.4` p. 1, `2.3.5` p. 1), and EPR's own note says its areas are
"approximate based on a design stage model and may not reflect the final as-built areas"
(Key Plans p. 9). **There is no measured survey of any building on the estate in the room.**

The area bases also conflict: Main House GIA reads 2,202 sqm on the standalone schedule
(Area Schedule row 33), 1,815 sqm on the brochure revision (Brochure p. 12), 3,855 sqm GIFA in the
cost report (Greenway p. 8) and 44,800 sq ft ≈ 4,162 sqm in Savills' existing-buildings table
(Savills p. 8). Any layout judgment should name which basis it is working on.

items.q: Is the kitchen sufficient? The Kitchen looks too small and in the wrong location, we also need to clarify the kitchen height
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL.** Location is answered, size and height are not.
body: **PARTIAL.** Location is answered, size and height are not.

The main kitchen sits in the **basement** of the Main House, in the north-east range, with kitchen
stores immediately east, private dining and a screening room adjacent, hotel stores to the north
and the boiler room, staff facility, wine cellars and the Vaults nearby; a second kitchen area
sits in the south-west annexe wing across the link corridor (Key Plans p. 8, key areas 1–11). The
ground-floor restaurant — Dining Room (3) and Print Room (4) — is directly above, with the lift
(12) beside it and the Great Hall (1) serving as reception (Key Plans p. 7).

EPR has already written the criticism onto the drawing: "**Very small kitchen — Relocate or
extend to 1**" against the basement kitchen (1 being the Back of House / current kitchen area),
"**Too far**" against the run from the basement kitchen out to the annexe, and "**Too small HK**"
against Housekeeping (Key Plans p. 8). The ground-floor annexe rooms carry "Finishing kitchen?"
(p. 7).

Missing: kitchen areas (the basement plan gives only a whole-floor GIA including tunnels),
**ceiling heights anywhere in any building**, equipment schedules, extract routes, and a measured
survey. Height cannot be resolved from the room.

items.q: Is the lift sufficient? Yes for the number of rooms, need to look at size of lfit and quality of lift and communication portal in lift.
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL.** Count and position are answered; specification is not. The Main House has **one**
body:
**PARTIAL.** Count and position are answered; specification is not. The Main House has **one**
lift, marked as key area (12) on the ground-floor plan beside the Dining Room and the annexe link
(Key Plans p. 7). The courtyard accommodation has none designed — the Stables upper-ground plan
carries EPR's annotation "**Need 1-2 lifts**" (Key Plans p. 12), which matters because 21 of the
43 courtyard keys are at upper-ground level (p. 12).

Nothing in the room states car size, capacity, speed, machine type, shaft dimensions, or any
communications provision.

items.q: Storage capacity?
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL.** Storage is located but nowhere quantified. Main House basement: Hotel stores,
body:
**PARTIAL.** Storage is located but nowhere quantified. Main House basement: Hotel stores,
Kitchen stores, Stores (6), wine cellars (10), the Vaults / wine tasting (8), and Housekeeping —
the last annotated "Too small HK" (Key Plans p. 8). Courtyard: the 2021 consented scheme provided
"a storage space at the northern end of the east range" of the North Courtyard, deliberately
placed there to address overlooking of the adjacent Old Forge property (JSA §8.3), plus waste and
recycling storage in the north courtyard (§13.7).

The problem is that the 2025 scheme takes those ranges for guest rooms, which is exactly what
EPR's own annotation asks: "WHERE DOES STAFF ACCOMMODATION & STORAGE GO NOW BEDROOMS IN NORTH
COURTYARD?" (Key Plans p. 11). **No storage areas appear anywhere in the area schedule.**

items.q: Back of house spaces?
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL, and the scheduled quantum looks light.** What is scheduled: "LODGES (STAFF FACILITIES
body:
**PARTIAL, and the scheduled quantum looks light.** What is scheduled: "LODGES (STAFF FACILITIES
+ BOH)" 709 sqm / 7,631.61 sq ft (Area Schedule rows 62–69) plus "The Stables BOH Building"
184 sqm / 1,980.56 sq ft (row 72) — **893 sqm / 9,612 sq ft in total**. Across 60 keys that is
about 160 sq ft per key, and it includes staff accommodation, not just working BOH.

items.statusLine: **JUDGMENT** — and an important one, because it is worth 709 sqm of new build in a Grade II*
body:
**JUDGMENT** — and an important one, because it is worth 709 sqm of new build in a Grade II*
registered park.

What is currently drawn on site: 709 sqm / 7,632 sq ft of staff facilities and BOH across the
North Lodge and its extension, **four new gatehouses** (2 × 90 sqm north, 2 × 90 sqm south), the
existing South Lodge and a new South Lodge (Area Schedule rows 62–69). The 2021 consented
alternative put "a full range of staff flats" in the North Courtyard's northern building, with
the east wing and the entirety of the west range also staff accommodation (JSA §8.2–8.3).

Two points the room adds. First, Historic England's stated test cuts directly at this: any
application must provide "a clear rationale outlining why the level of accommodation provided is
necessary **and explaining the merits of providing it in the courtyards as opposed to within the
house or in cottages/lodges scattered within the grounds**" (JSA Appendix II, p. 25) — the
on-site/off-site question is a heritage-justification question, not only an operational one.
Second, four new-build gatehouses in a Grade II* registered park is a consent ask in its own
right and none of them is consented.

What "the schedule" is: an **area** schedule, GIA by space, dated 02/06/2025, rev B 10/07/2025

items.statusLine: **PARTIAL — clearer than the question assumes at estate level, and unresolved at the level that
body:
**PARTIAL — clearer than the question assumes at estate level, and unresolved at the level that
matters.**

The masterplan is colour-coded **New Build / Existing / Consented** across the whole estate
(Masterplan p. 1; Brochure p. 7). Reading it with the area schedule:

- **New build:** two north gatehouses and two south gatehouses (4 × 90 sqm = 360 sqm, rows
  65–66); North Lodge Extension 75 sqm (row 64); New South Lodge 60 sqm (row 68); the **New
  Concert Hall two-storey extension 529 sqm** (row 60); the Proposed South Wing; the new
  loggia/pergola; plus temporary structures — Regatta pavilion 500 sqm (row 75), floating
  restaurant 75 sqm (row 74), "various events marquees — tbc" (Brochure p. 12).
- **Consented (23/07590/LBC):** North Courtyard, South Courtyard, and the driveway
  (Masterplan pp. 1–2).
- **Existing / refurbishment:** Main House, Riding House, Chapel, the Concert Hall shell
  (471 sqm), North and South Lodges, the Stables.
What is **not** clear, and should be raised:

- The courtyards are labelled "Consented", but what is consented there is estate offices, staff
  accommodation and storage (LBC p. 1; JSA §5.1, §8.2–8.3), while the 2025 scheme puts **43 guest
  rooms** in them — "20 Guest rooms - new build" in the North Courtyard and "23 Guest rooms -
  amend existing build" in the South (Masterplan CK). That is a change of use and, in the North
  Courtyard, largely new build. The FUL that would govern it is absent.
- The Concert Hall is more new build than refurbishment (529 sqm new against 471 sqm existing) —
  material for both cost and consent.
- The seven older "Consented" labels on the masterplan (South Buildings and New Access) describe
  permissions whose **commencement deadlines have all passed** — the latest 26 April 2021
  (cluster index B, vision mop-up). Unless lawfully implemented, they are lapsed, and nothing in
  the room evidences implementation either way.

| Residential consultancy | **Savills Global Residential Development Consultancy** (Rosie Tucker MRICS; Louis Keighley MRICS) | Savills pp. 1–3 |

**Not evidenced anywhere in the room:** catering, acoustic, **fire**, building control / approved
inspector, utilities, access roads, river wall, AV, PDBR. Note that the question's parenthetical
"**fire (already on board)**" is not corroborated by a single document in the data room — no fire
engineer is named, no fire strategy exists, and no building control correspondence is present.
Worth confirming on the call rather than assuming.

Also note: every one of the named reports above **exists but is not in the data room**. They are
a discrete, well-defined ask (see the outstanding register below), and several of them —
structural appraisal, buildings survey, FRA, ecology, contamination — are exactly the documents
that would otherwise have to be re-commissioned at the buyer's cost.

items.q: Is the current house sufficiently completed with FFE?
items.statusLine: **PARTIAL.** The only quantified FF&E in the room is historic and modest: within Greenway's key
body:
**PARTIAL.** The only quantified FF&E in the room is historic and modest: within Greenway's key
client costs, **Furniture, Furnishings & Equipment £450,000** and **Operating Equipment
£250,000**, with **Art & Sculpture EXCLUDED** (Greenway p. 6) — £450k across 3,855 sqm of Grade I
Main House, priced as part of the works that brought the building to its current state. That is
a private-house allowance, not a hotel FF&E position.

The 25 internal photographs show the principal rooms furnished — Great Hall, Library (four
images), Gibbons Room (three), Wyatt Room (three), Dining Room, Marble, Persian, Venetian and
Chinese Rooms, the Grand Stair, Print Room, two bedrooms and the Alda Freeman Suite bathrooms —
but they are catalogued by filename only and were not reviewed against any list (cluster index E).

**No FF&E inventory, schedule, valuation, condition report or chattels list is in the room, and
nothing states what would be included in a sale.** Given the house is presented furnished and
the vendor is a Jersey company holding a Grade I house with art and antiques, the chattels
position is a real commercial question, not a fit-out detail.

items.q: What else is needed - reception pods for example?

body:
**JUDGMENT / NOT IN ROOM.** The room fixes where reception happens — the Great Hall (1) is
labelled "Reception" on the Main House ground floor (Key Plans p. 7) and a separate Reception (5)
sits at the courtyard guest-room entrance in the Stables (p. 11) — and specifies nothing about
how it is furnished or fitted. No FF&E specification exists for any space.

items.q: What assumption should we make for the new bedrooms - is there sufficient in the cost schedule for this? What cost schedule? We can refer to our lux cost assessments for this?

body:
**PARTIAL.** On "what cost schedule" — there is none; see Hotel Development item 4 above. So
there is nothing in which an FF&E allowance for new bedrooms could be either present or absent.

What the room does give, and it is enough to apply a per-key or per-sqm allowance: the full room
schedule and mix. Main House 17 keys — 1 Principal Suite (6%), 2 One Bed Suites (12%), 4 Junior
Suites (23%), 10 Guestrooms (59%), ranging 36–135 sqm (Key Plans p. 9; Area Schedule rows 14–32).
Courtyard/Stables 43 keys — 22 at ground level (20 guest rooms 45–50 sqm, 2 suites 60–80 sqm) and
21 at upper ground (16 guest rooms, 5 suites), individual areas 45–72 sqm (Key Plans pp. 11–12;
Area Schedule rows 37–54). Average key size is stated as ">55 sqm" (Brochure p. 4).

items.q: Is there FFE for the outside spaces as well in the cost schedule? What cost schedule?
items.statusLine: **NOT IN ROOM.** No cost schedule, and no external FF&E line anywhere. Greenway's only external
body:
**NOT IN ROOM.** No cost schedule, and no external FF&E line anywhere. Greenway's only external
line is "Localised Landscaping & External Works, 1 item, £2,000,000" (Greenway p. 8) — historic,
Main-House-adjacent, unbroken down, and not FF&E.

The room does identify the external spaces that will need it, with areas: East / river view F&B
terrace 138 sqm, South / parkland view F&B terrace 190 sqm, Banquetting House loggia 100 sqm,
riverside floating restaurant 75 sqm, Regatta temporary pavilion 500 sqm at 200–500 pax
(Area Schedule rows 10, 11, 74, 75, 77), plus the new loggia/pergola and reinstated loggia
(Masterplan p. 1) and "various events marquees — tbc" (Brochure p. 12).

halves.intro:
*Classified separately, per the second-half convention: **JUDGMENT** marks a question that is a
decision for Align, the operator or a consultant rather than a document request. The room
evidence bearing on each is still set out, because most of these are answerable further than the
question assumes.*

**Before the section: almost every question here is answerable from one document.** The EPR key
plans (`3.3.1`, 10 July 2025) locate the kitchen, the lift, back of house, storage, the
washrooms, the offices, the staff canteen, the courtyard walk, the media room and study, and the
parking zone — and carry the consultant's own red annotations against most of them. The document
is in the room and the mark-ups are already on it.

askIntro:
*Everything below is genuinely absent from the data room. Ordered by what unblocks the most work.
Items marked **named** are documents the room proves exist, because a vendor-side document cites
them by title and author — those should be the easiest to obtain and the first to be asked for.*

items.text: **23/07589/FUL — the decision notice, conditions, plans list and any section 106.** The listed building consent is in the room; its full planning companion is not. Without it there is no evidence of a lawful hotel or guest-accommodation use, and the conditions that normally carry ecology, highways, parking, drainage, landscape and hours of operation are unseen.

**The approved drawing set for 23/07590/LBC**, listed by number in condition 2: 21-01/A; PL300D–PL306C; PL320C–PL322B; PV300B–PV314; PV327–PV340; SL10C–SL12B; SL326A–SL330. PL306 alone answers the washroom question; PL301/PL306/PV327–339 answer the pool, gym and spa.
**Evidence of commencement and condition discharge** for 23/07590/LBC — conditions 3, 6 and 7 are pre-commencement gates and the consent lapses **6 December 2027**.

**Implementation evidence for the seven older consents** (15/05907, 15/05908, 17/05210, 17/05211, 18/05598, 18/05599, 15/07051), whose commencement deadlines have all passed. The masterplan labels them "Consented"; unless lawfully commenced they are lapsed.
**21/05417/FUL** — riverbank erosion works, on the public record, not in the room.

**Pre-application paperwork for the residential scheme.** Savills reports discussions "so far, well-received" (p. 7) with nothing behind it. This sentence carries the enabling-development case; it needs the officer's note or letter.
**Pre-application paperwork for the 2023 applications and the 2025 EPR 60-key scheme.** The only pre-app document in the room is the Historic England letter of 5 July 2010.

askGroups.title: The named reports — they exist, they are cited, they are not in the room

items.text: **Structural Engineering Appraisal**, *Courtyard Buildings and Gatehouse*, **Alan Baxter and Associates** (named, JSA §2.6).
**Buildings Survey Report**, **William Martin & Partners LLP** (named, JSA §2.5).
**Flood Risk Assessment and Drainage Strategy**, **RAB**, February 2021 — including **Section 5.4** (the SuDS sizing) and **Section 4.1** (the 33.22 mAOD finished floor level) (named, JSA §2.7).
**Ecological Scoping Survey**, **Aspect Ecology**, and the update by **Catherine Bickmore** (named, JSA §13.4) — with confirmation of whether bat emergence/activity surveys were done.
**Phase 1 Contamination Assessment**, **Opus Joynes Pike** (named, JSA §13.5).
**Energy Report**, **Ecovision** (named, JSA §3.5).
**Type 3 Asbestos Survey** for the courtyards (named, JSA §14.9), plus any Main House asbestos survey, register or clearance certificates.
**BS5837 tree survey** (referred to, JSA §2.9, §3.4).
**Fawley Court Conservation Plan Vols 1–3** (Dr Sarah Rutherford) and the **Historic Building Survey of Service Buildings** (Kirsty Rodwell) (named, JSA §1.3, §2.4).

askGroups.title: The flood question — the single biggest unevidenced assumption

items.text: **The Environment Agency evidence for the re-mapped flood zones.** Savills' 12-unit scheme assumes "the existing masterplan is incorrect and the floodplains are far smaller than is currently shown… currently being updated by the environment agency" (pp. 47, 50). The only primary evidence in the room says **Flood Zone 3** with a 33.22 mAOD floor-level requirement (RAB, quoted at JSA §2.7). A date, a reference or a revised zone plan is needed. Until it exists, the residential limb rests on hearsay.

askGroups.title: Building condition and services — nothing exists

items.text: Fire strategy, fire risk assessment, and the building control record with any completion certificates.
Fire systems: fire stopping, alarm, emergency lighting and signage, sprinklers — specification and commissioning records.
Fire door survey; window schedule and condition survey (Main House); roof condition survey (Main House); flue and fireplace survey.

MEP survey of existing systems, with a breakdown of the £5.59m MEP allowance and any outstanding works — specifically whether the part-implemented water-source heat pump (JSA §3.5) has been completed.
CCTV and security systems: extent, age, monitoring arrangement.

**Acoustic testing** — internal (room-to-room, corridor, floor) and external (A4155 road noise at the Meadows). Neither exists, and both are assumed in the room: Savills' pricing depends on "extensive acoustic tests and noise cancellation strategies" already having reduced road noise (p. 47).

**Measured survey.** Every plan in the room is approximate, several are drawn from proposed rather than as-built information, and the Main House area basis varies from 1,815 sqm to 4,162 sqm across four documents. Nothing can be scaled.

askGroups.title: Utilities, infrastructure and the estate edge

items.text: Utility capacity statements and incoming supply records: power (DNO position and any connection agreement), gas, potable water, telecoms.

Foul drainage: cess pit locations, capacities, tankering frequency and cost, discharge consents — and a position on capacity for 60 keys plus 12 houses plus events, given "no proposed change to the current foul sewage drainage system" (JSA §2.8).
**River wall and bank condition assessment**, and the EA permitting position for works to the bank. The masterplan states "Long water banks to be strengthened" with nothing behind it.
Dredging: any survey of the Long Water, the inlet or the river frontage — a floating restaurant is scheduled at 75 sqm.
Transport assessment / traffic survey. Nothing exists, and Savills records queuing on the A4155 outside the main entrance (p. 10).
**Parking strategy with space counts.** The only counted figure in the room is **11 spaces**, sized in 2021 for a scheme with 15 guest rooms.
**Premises licence(s)**, temporary event notices used to date, and the licensing history for the Regatta pavilion, weddings and events. Nothing licensing-related is in the room.
**Operator position:** confirmation of where the brand discussion stands, whether Belmond remains preferred, and what "NoMad Hotel" on the EPR title blocks refers to.
**FF&E inventory / chattels list**, and what is included in a sale.
**Reconciled key count.** The room prints 60 (EPR), 65 (Savills p. 9) and, with the South Wing's nine bedrooms, an implied 69. One number is needed before anything is costed.
**Reconciled area schedule.** The two revisions disagree on the Main House by 387 sqm and on whether a 127 sqm new-wing ballroom exists.
**A resolved staff accommodation and storage strategy** — the consented location is being converted to bedrooms, and EPR itself asks the question on its own drawing.
Confirmation of the residential **tenure** basis: Savills assumes 999-year leaseholds (p. 47) against the deal's freehold assumption.

**There is no forward cost plan in the data room.** No elemental estimate, no budget, no cost schedule for the hotel, the new build, the infrastructure, the landscape, the M&E, the residences or the FF&E. The only cost document is Greenway's historic Main House estimate. Confirm on the call that none exists, so nobody keeps looking.

Substantiation of the Greenway £45.79m: invoices, contracts, completion certificates and warranties — and the equivalent record for the buildings Greenway excludes (Riding School, courtyard, chapel, gate houses, perimeter and security, waterway, Capability Brown landscape, and the demolitions already carried out).

closing:
Read plainly: **13% of the list is settled by the room, 48% is part-settled, 30% is genuinely
outstanding** and 9% is a decision rather than a document. The large partial category is the
useful finding — in most cases the room gives the location, the area or the named report, and
what is missing is the measurement, the cost or the document itself.

docIntro:
Cross-check run 16 August 2026. Source question list: `Qs for Fawley - Hotel Development.pdf`
(4pp). Every question in that document is reproduced below in its original order and section
structure, and tagged against what the vendor's data room actually contains.

**Tags**

- **ANSWERED** — the room settles it, with the answer and a doc + page citation.
- **PARTIAL** — the room gives part of it; what is given and what is missing are both stated.
- **NOT IN ROOM** — genuinely outstanding; these form the ask list at the end.
- **JUDGMENT** — used only in the second half ("Qs for Align Partners Call"). The question is
  a decision for Align or a consultant, not a document request; the room evidence bearing on
  it is set out, then the call is named as a call.

**Two things to carry before reading**

1. **Several of these "questions" are transcriptions of mark-ups already on documents inside
   the data room.** `3.3.1 EPR Hotel Key Plans` and `Fawley Court - Masterplan CK version.pdf`
   both carry red annotations — "Very small kitchen — Relocate or extend to 1", "Too far",
